idea_name: Cross-layer KV sharing as hierarchical pattern sensor
mechanism: MLKV shares Key-Value heads not only within a Self-Attention layer (GQA/MQA) but across successive Transformer layers, motivated by the observation that adjacent layers compute similar targets: lower layers capture superficial patterns and upper layers capture more semantic detail, so attention can be delegated across layer groups while FeedForward keeps level-specific computation.
data_needed: Multimodal bar-history tensor (price + indicators) for EURUSD H1; multi-layer Transformer encoder/attention stack with configurable heads_kv and layers_to_one_kv
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train 2023; test January 2023 (article text)
why_new_for_mis: Treats layer depth as a hierarchy of market-pattern granularity and makes that hierarchy an explicit, shareable sensing substrate—MIS can read superficial vs semantic regime cues from which KV block is active rather than only from final embeddings.
quote: the lower levels deal with superficial patterns, and the upper levels deal with more semantic details. Thus, it can be concluded that attention can be delegated to groups of layers while keeping the necessary computations in the FeedForward block.

mechanism: Actor and Critic use a multi-layer cross-attention block (CNeuronMLCrossAttentionMLKV) that compares an account-state embedding to the Environmental State Encoder’s forecast tensor; Query heads=8, KV heads=2, new KV every 3 of 9 nested layers—fusing portfolio/context with predicted price path under memory-efficient shared KV.
data_needed: AccountDescr vector (balance/equity/positions), Encoder NForecast×BarDescr (or latent) forecast, historical interaction trajectories
why_new_for_mis: Frames sensing as explicit cross-attention between account/context state and a multi-step market forecast, giving MIS a template for context-conditioned sequence sensors rather than price-only encoders.
quote: This layer will compare the current account state with the forecast of the upcoming price movement obtained from the Environment State Encoder.

mechanism: Coarser-Scale Construction Module (CSCM) maps inputs through an FC alignment then stacked FCNN blocks: each block extracts vectors with a given cross-step, concatenates them, convolves, and feeds the next block to build coarser temporal scales; multi-scale features are concatenated and linearly projected back to input length, forming a pyramidal feature tree.
data_needed: Univariate or multimodal time series of length inputs_count with variables channels; user-specified convolution windows per FCNN level
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic time-series forecasting setup in this part; live FX test deferred to Part 97
why_new_for_mis: Gives MIS an explicit multi-scale feature tree (fine→coarse) built by successive cross-step convolutions, usable as a regime/structure sensor over any instrument/timeframe bar tensor.
quote: The CSCM module constructs a tree of features of the analyzed time series. ... Each of them, using the results of the previous block as input, extracts features of a larger scale.

mechanism: Skip-Pyramidal Attention Module processes a temporal feature tree with intra-scale attention (node↔neighbors in same layer) and inter-scale attention (node↔parent); lower levels focus on short-term detailed patterns, upper levels on macroscopic trends and periodicities (e.g., every Monday, month start), adapting to short-term fluctuations and long-term evolutions.
data_needed: Pyramidal feature tree from CSCM over historical bars; attention across PAM levels
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Generic time-series; periodic examples Monday/month-start; FX evaluation in Part 97
why_new_for_mis: Directly senses regime-like structure by separating short-horizon microstructure from macro/periodic trend attention on one feature tree—useful for MIS regime and calendar-periodicity sensing.
quote: At lower levels, the model may focus on short-term, detailed patterns. The upper levels are able to capture more macroscopic trends and periodicities. The proposed Skip-PAM pays more attention to periodic dependencies such as every Monday or the beginning of each month.

idea_name: Learned S3 feature permutation per pyramid level
mechanism: Instead of authors’ fixed steps between features within an attention level, an S3 mixing/permutation layer is placed before each Skip-PAM level so the model learns which features each attention pyramid analyzes at that level; attention window shrinks with level (iPAMLayers−l) creating a pyramid.
data_needed: Multimodal feature sequence after CSCM; per-level S3 + Q/KV projections; PAM layer count
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Implementation article; instrument/timeframe tested in Part 97 (EURUSD H1)
why_new_for_mis: Turns multi-scale attention topology into a learned sensor: which lag/feature alignments matter at each granularity is data-driven, not a fixed Monday/month grid.
quote: What if we let the model learn on its own which features each individual attention pyramid will analyze at each individual attention level? ... We'll just add a S3 layer before each attention level.

mechanism: MH2PyrAttentionOut computes SoftMax dependence scores only inside a local attention window (abs(k−q_id)≤delta_win); outside-window scores are forced to 0, and the window shrinks at higher PAM levels—localizing sequence sensing while reusing standard attention gradient kernels.
data_needed: Q and KV tensors per PAM level; window size derived from remaining pyramid depth
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: Sequence models generally; applied later on EURUSD H1
why_new_for_mis: Provides a local multi-scale sequence sensor that ignores distant tokens outside a shrinking window—useful for MIS when global attention would mix incompatible regimes.
quote: we calculate the dependence coefficients only within the attention window of the current element. For all other elements, the dependence coefficient is "0". ... at each subsequent level, we reduce the attention window, thereby creating a pyramid effect.

mechanism: Environmental State Encoder is trained to forecast upcoming price movement and analyzed indicator values together; indicators (overbought/oversold, trend strength, reversal cues) are smoother digital-filter transforms of noisy price, so predicting them refines/confirms the price-path forecast.
data_needed: HistoryBars×BarDescr raw OHLC+indicator state tensor; NForecast-step targets of the same BarDescr channels; EURUSD H1 trajectories
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; train full year 2023; test January 2024
why_new_for_mis: Treats smoother indicator channels as co-predicted sensing targets that corroborate noisy price forecasts—MIS can use dual-head continuation error as a confirmation/regime-consistency signal.
quote: By predicting the subsequent values of these indicators, we aim to refine and confirm our forecasts of price movements.

idea_name: CSCM windows 6/5/4 then Skip-PAM encoder stack
mechanism: Encoder: raw HistoryBars×BarDescr → batch norm → CSCM with three FCNN scales windows {6,5,4} on transposed univariate series → three Skip-PAM (MLKV) layers (Q heads 8, KV heads 4, entity dim 32, 3 pyramid levels each) → transpose → per-series conv MLP to NForecast → RevIN denorm → FreDF.
data_needed: BarDescr features per bar, HistoryBars lookback, NForecast horizon; constants synchronized train/deploy
why_new_for_mis: Concrete multi-scale sequence encoder recipe MIS can reuse as a market-state sensor: fixed 6/5/4 bar coarser scales plus pyramidal Skip-PAM before forecasting.
quote: We will extract features in 3 levels with analysis window sizes of 6, 5 and 4 bars. ... we will add 3 consecutive Skip-PAM layers with the same configuration.

idea_name: BatchNorm plus TANH one-sigma forecast gate
mechanism: Inputs are batch-normalized to near-zero mean/unit variance; forecast MLP ends in TANH so outputs lie in (−1,1), covering ~68% of a normal variable within one standard deviation and filtering outliers beyond 1σ—deliberately not fitting all noisy fluctuations.
data_needed: Raw bar/indicator series with non-stationary means/variances; batch stats from training (batch≈1e4)
why_new_for_mis: Casts volatility/noise control as a sensing prior: predict within one-sigma mass and treat extremes as noise to ignore—useful for MIS robust regime forecasting under fat tails.
quote: using TANH, which has a value range of (-1, 1), allows us to cover 68% of the analyzed variable's values while filtering outliers that fall beyond one standard deviation from the mean.

idea_name: Encoder latent as trend-strength environment state
mechanism: Actor/Critic do not consume denormalized Encoder outputs (which re-add series statistics); they attend to a hidden/latent Encoder layer so predicted paths are free of raw-data biases—author states the goal is to extract current trends and their strength in that hidden state.
data_needed: Trained MSFformer Encoder; LatentLayer index; account/action tensors for Actor/Critic
why_new_for_mis: Defines a latent trend-and-strength sensor distinct from reconstructed prices—MIS can monitor Encoder hidden state as a regime embedding rather than forecast levels alone.
quote: To achieve maximum results, we need to extract current trends in the state of the environment and their strength in the hidden state of the Encoder, which is then accessed by the Actor and Critic models.

mechanism: Each sampled state appends a 4-D time embedding: sin of normalized year fraction (2023–2024), cos of month-period phase, sin of week-period phase, sin of day-period phase—injecting calendar multi-scale phase into Actor account features.
data_needed: Bar/account timestamp; PeriodSeconds for MN1/W1/D1; year anchor dates
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1 trajectories with account[7] time field
why_new_for_mis: Supplies explicit multi-horizon calendar-phase sensing aligned with Skip-PAM’s periodic focus—MIS can fuse these harmonics with price features for session/week/month regime cues.
quote: we also encode the time stamp, which we will represent as a vector of sinusoidal harmonics of different frequencies.

idea_name: Stochastic policy variance as uncertainty sensor
mechanism: VAE-style stochastic Actor head emits actions from a learned mean/variance normal; when the action is well determined variance→0 and output≈mean; as uncertainty rises, action variance rises—test-time pass-to-pass dispersion diagnoses under-trained or unstable policy/environment fit.
data_needed: Actor latent parameters for NActions means/variances; repeated Strategy Tester passes
instruments_and_timeframes_in_article: EURUSD H1; January 2024 test (37 trades in reported run)
why_new_for_mis: Turns policy noise into an explicit market/decision uncertainty sensor—MIS can track rising action variance as a regime-change or model-disagreement warning.
quote: Under ideal conditions, where an action can be precisely determined, the variance of the distribution for the generated action approaches zero. ... As uncertainty increases, so does the variance of the generated actions.

mechanism: After per-horizon direct forecasts (assumed independent), a FreDF layer with probability 0.7 reconciles steps of the predicted multimodal series in the frequency domain so successive forecast bars respect time-series dependence rather than independent step noise.
data_needed: NForecast×BarDescr forecast tensor from Encoder MLP; FreDF probability hyperparameter
why_new_for_mis: Adds a sequence-coherence sensor/constraint on multi-step forecasts—MIS can use FreDF residual/spectrum as a measure of internally inconsistent predicted paths.
quote: the paradigm of direct forecasting assumes the independence of individual steps in the predicted sequence. ... we will leverage the advancements introduced by the FreDF method to reconcile the individual steps within the predicted sequence
